title: Famous brands and their stories
examples: How does a company decide what its brand story should be?
Can a logo change too much and still be recognized?
What is the difference between a product and a brand?

explain.say: Today we are learning about building a strong brand.

items: Idea 2: How is a brand built?
Idea 3: What role do logos play?

draw.text: Building a Brand: Story, Logo, Trust

explain.say: A brand is more than just a product you buy.
Companies build a brand by telling a consistent story.
Logos are simple pictures that help people remember the brand.
Trust is the feeling people have when they buy from you.
In everyday life, think about your favourite snack brand.

faq.q: Why do companies care so much about their logos?
faq.a: Logos act as a quick visual reminder of the brand. They help people instantly recognize what you are selling.
asks: What is the purpose of a company logo?
Do logos help people remember a brand?

faq.q: Is a good story the same as a good advertisement?
faq.a: No, a story is the overall reason for being. An advertisement is just one way to tell that story.
asks: Can a story be different from marketing?

faq.q: How long does it take to build trust with customers?
faq.a: Building trust takes a long time and requires consistent good actions. It can be lost very quickly.
asks: What makes customers trust a brand?

faq.q: If a company changes its logo, does that hurt its brand?
faq.a: It can, if the change is too sudden or confusing. The brand story must support the new look.
asks: How big of a logo change is okay?

faq.q: What makes a brand story unique?
faq.a: A unique story comes from the company's real purpose or the problem it solves. It should feel genuine.
asks: Where does a brand story come from?
Should a brand story be exciting?

facts: A brand is the overall feeling people have about a company.
A brand story explains the 'why' behind the company's existence.
Logos must be simple enough to be recognized quickly.
Trust is built over time through consistent quality.

quiz.say: A company that always delivers on time is building which element of its brand?
quiz.why: Reliability is a key part of keeping the promise, which builds trust.

wrong.1: A logo is just a picture; it does not describe the actual service.
wrong.2: The story explains the 'why', but reliability is the proof.
wrong.3: The product is what is sold, but trust is the feeling around it.

quiz.say: If a company's story is about helping the environment, what should its logo reflect?
quiz.why: The logo should visually match the core message of the brand story.

wrong.0: Complex designs are hard to remember and might look messy.
wrong.1: While abstract, the shape should still hint at the brand's purpose.
wrong.3: Neon colours often suggest excitement, not necessarily environmental care.

quiz.say: Which element is the most important for a brand to maintain over many years?
quiz.why: Consistency across story, logo, and quality keeps trust high.

wrong.0: Too many changes confuse customers and break recognition.
wrong.1: Endorsements are temporary; the brand itself must be solid.
wrong.3: Money helps, but it cannot replace a genuine, consistent message.
